MOB_STYLE:
CHARACTER:

A hostile cave spider enemy from a grim dark medieval fantasy MMORPG.

BODY:

- low flat spider body
- broad dark abdomen
- smaller cephalothorax
- tense predatory stance
- eight long articulated legs

CARAPACE:

- dark desaturated charcoal-black
- dirty dark gray-brown secondary tones
- faint oily sheen
- restrained bristle texture

HEAD:

- compact spider head
- multiple hostile dark-red eyes in a cluster
- tiny eye highlights
- dark chelicerae with visible fangs
- no separate neck

LEGS:

- exactly EIGHT anatomical legs total
- four on each side
- long, thin, jointed
- dark with subtle banding at the joints
- small hooked claws at the tips

ABDOMEN:

- large rounded abdomen
- subtle darker markings
- spinnerets at the rear
- no tail

OUTLINE — HARD REQUIREMENT:

- draw a thin, crisp, continuous dark outline around the ENTIRE body silhouette
- outline every leg from the body to the claw tip
- outline the head, cephalothorax, abdomen and all eight legs
- the outline must be visibly darker than the charcoal carapace
- the outline must NOT merge separate legs together
- each leg must have a clear, closed contour with visible separation from the body and from other legs
- no leg may blend into the background or into the body without a boundary

MOOD:

- hostile
- predatory
- skittering
- grim
- dangerous

Do not make the spider:

- cute
- friendly
- plush
- magical
- undead
- mutated
- insect-like with only six legs- insect-like with only six legs

CHROMA SPILL — HARD REQUIREMENT:

- ABSOLUTELY NO chroma-key green color (#00FF00) may appear ON the spider
- no green tint, green edge, green decoration, or green glow on the body, head, abdomen, eyes, fangs, or any leg
- no green color in the GAPS between legs and the body
- no green triangles, dots, or shapes anywhere inside the spider silhouette
- the connection point where each leg meets the body must be solid dark carapace, NOT green
- every gap between a leg and the body, and between adjacent legs, must be filled with dark charcoal/black outline, never green
- the only green in the image is the uniform background matte
- if any green appears on the creature, the result is REJECTED
MOB_ANATOMY:
ANATOMY INTEGRITY — HARD REQUIREMENT:

The spider has exactly EIGHT anatomical legs total.

Four legs on each side of the body.

Every visible leg must remain attached to the cephalothorax.

When a leg moves, move the ENTIRE LEG including the claw.

STRICTLY FORBIDDEN:

- detached leg
- floating leg
- duplicate leg
- ghost leg
- extra leg
- missing leg
- six-legged insect body
- disconnected foot
- residual old limb fragment
- extra pair of legs growing from the abdomen
MASTER_FRONT_LEFT_PROMPT:
Create one isolated fantasy cave spider enemy.

CAMERA AND PROJECTION:

Use one fixed classic three-quarter isometric game camera.

The camera is elevated above the creature and looks downward
at a consistent angle.

Use orthographic dimetric projection compatible with classic
2-to-1 isometric game tiles.

There is NO perspective convergence.

Preserve exactly:

- camera elevation
- camera angle
- projection
- zoom
- apparent creature scale

This is NOT:

- strict side profile
- direct top-down
- eye-level view
- cinematic perspective

ORIENTATION:

The spider faces diagonally toward SCREEN LOWER-LEFT.

Its head points lower-left.

Its abdomen extends upper-right.

This is a THREE-QUARTER FRONT-AND-SIDE VIEW.

The viewer sees:

- head
- eye cluster
- fangs
- cephalothorax
- side of abdomen
- upper surface of abdomen
- all eight legs
- spinnerets

WALK_SW:
WALK CONTACT A — STRONG READABLE STRIDE.

Near-side FRONT leg:

- extend clearly toward SCREEN LOWER-LEFT
- move the claw at least one full leg length beyond idle
- claw clearly projects past the head

Far-side FRONT leg:

- pull backward beneath the cephalothorax

Near-side MIDDLE leg:

- move forward
- bend visibly

Far-side MIDDLE leg:

- extend clearly backward toward SCREEN UPPER-RIGHT

Near-side REAR leg:

- step forward

Far-side REAR leg:

- extend backward

BODY:

- shoulders shift forward
- abdomen counter-shifts
- weight distribution changes

This limb arrangement must remain obvious
after 96x96 reduction.

PRIORITY ORDER — NON-NEGOTIABLE:

1. MOVE all eight legs to the pose described above. This is the FIRST priority.
2. PRESERVE the same character (dark charcoal body, red eye cluster, segmentation). This is the SECOND priority.
3. Do NOT change eyes, body texture, fangs, carapace markings, or color palette.
4. The ONLY changes between this frame and the previous frame must be the eight legs moving into the pose above.
5. If you must choose between an authentic walk pose and perfect identity preservation, choose the walk pose. Identity is preserved by the color palette and silhouette, not by micro-texture.

DO NOT merely redraw the same idle spider with shifted eyes or added spots. That is forbidden.

WALK PASSING A — STRONG MID-SWING FRAME.

THIS MUST NOT LOOK LIKE CONTACT A.

THIS MUST NOT LOOK LIKE CONTACT B.

Near-side FRONT leg:

- lift the ENTIRE claw clearly OFF the ground
- lift the leg vertically by a clearly visible amount
- create a visible chroma-green gap beneath the leg
- bend joint
- move the leg backward beneath the head

Far-side FRONT leg:

- swing the ENTIRE leg clearly forward toward SCREEN LOWER-LEFT
- extend joint
- move claw toward future contact point
- claw is NOT planted yet

Near-side MIDDLE leg:

- lift and pass beneath abdomen
- visibly change joint angle

Far-side MIDDLE leg:

- recover forward beneath the body

Near-side REAR leg:

- lift and pass beneath abdomen

Far-side REAR leg:

- recover forward

BODY:

- body rises clearly above contact pose
- abdomen rises
- center of weight moves between both contact phases

CRITICAL 96x96 READABILITY:

The lifted leg MUST remain visibly separated from the ground
after reduction to 96x96.

Do NOT merely shift the leg a few pixels.

Move the WHOLE limb.

PRIORITY ORDER — NON-NEGOTIABLE:

1. MOVE all eight legs to the pose described above. This is the FIRST priority.
2. PRESERVE the same character. This is the SECOND priority.
3. Do NOT change eyes, body texture, fangs, carapace markings.
4. The ONLY changes between this frame and the previous frame must be the eight legs in the lifted/swinging pose.
5. If you must choose between an authentic walk pose and perfect identity preservation, choose the walk pose.

DO NOT merely redraw the same idle spider with shifted eyes. That is forbidden.

WALK CONTACT B — CLEAR OPPOSITE STRIDE.

Far-side FRONT leg:

- extend forward toward SCREEN LOWER-LEFT

Near-side FRONT leg:

- pull backward beneath head

Far-side MIDDLE leg:

- move forward

Near-side MIDDLE leg:

- extend backward toward SCREEN UPPER-RIGHT

Far-side REAR leg:

- move forward

Near-side REAR leg:

- extend backward

Reverse the diagonal limb arrangement from Contact A.

The silhouette must visibly differ from Contact A.

PRIORITY ORDER — NON-NEGOTIABLE:

1. MOVE all eight legs into the OPPOSITE stride from Contact A. This is the FIRST priority.
2. PRESERVE the same character. This is the SECOND priority.
3. Do NOT merely redraw Contact A with shifted eyes.

WALK PASSING B — STRONG OPPOSITE MID-SWING FRAME.

THIS MUST NOT LOOK LIKE CONTACT B.

THIS MUST NOT LOOK LIKE CONTACT A.

Far-side FRONT leg:

- lift the ENTIRE claw clearly OFF the ground
- create a visible chroma-green gap beneath the lifted leg
- bend joint
- retract beneath head

Near-side FRONT leg:

- swing clearly forward toward SCREEN LOWER-LEFT
- extend joint
- claw approaches next contact
- claw is NOT planted yet

Far-side MIDDLE leg:

- lift and pass beneath abdomen

Near-side MIDDLE leg:

- recover forward

Far-side REAR leg:

- lift and pass beneath abdomen

Near-side REAR leg:

- recover forward

BODY:

- body rises clearly above contact pose
- abdomen rises
- center of weight moves between both contact phases

CRITICAL 96x96 READABILITY:

The lifted leg MUST remain visibly separated from the ground.

Move the WHOLE limb.

Do NOT merely shift the leg.

PRIORITY ORDER — NON-NEGOTIABLE:

1. MOVE all eight legs into the OPPOSITE mid-swing pose. This is the FIRST priority.
2. PRESERVE the same character. This is the SECOND priority.
3. Do NOT merely redraw Contact A or Contact B with shifted eyes.
ATTACK_SW:
ATTACK ANTICIPATION.

Crouch lower.

Compress all eight legs.

Pull head and fangs backward.

Fangs angle upward.

Abdomen raises slightly.

ATTACK WIND-UP.

Stronger compression.

Rear legs load.

Head retracts.

Chelicerae spread.

Fangs begin parting.

ATTACK LUNGE.

Hind legs push.

Body stretches strongly toward SCREEN LOWER-LEFT.

Head and fangs thrust forward.

Front legs reach.

Fangs open wide.

ATTACK IMPACT / BITE.

Maximum forward extension.

Fangs visible and forward.

Front legs extended.

Body elongated.

No target.

No blood.

No VFX.

ATTACK RECOIL.

Head retracts.

Legs retract.

Body shortens.

Fangs close.

ATTACK RECOVERY.

Return toward combat idle.

Legs settle.

Head settles.

Abdomen settles.
HIT_VARIANTS:
DAMAGE REACTION A — IMPACT.

Hit from front-left.

Head snaps backward.

Near front leg lifts clearly.

Body compresses.

Legs brace.

Spider remains alive.

DAMAGE REACTION A — PEAK STAGGER.

Body twists away.

Lifted leg remains displaced.

One middle leg slides.

Clearly different from previous frame.

DAMAGE REACTION A — RECOVERY.

Leg returns toward support.

Body untwists.

Head rises.

Keep residual stagger.

Do not make this identical to idle.

DAMAGE REACTION B — IMPACT.

Side impact.

Body jerks sideways.

Opposite front leg lifts.

One middle leg steps outward.

Head dips.

Spider remains alive.

DAMAGE REACTION B — PEAK.

Front half drops.

One foreleg bends strongly.

Opposite foreleg reaches for balance.

Abdomen remains slightly raised.

DAMAGE REACTION B — RECOVERY.

Body rises.

Legs return toward support.

Middle leg steps inward.

Head lifts.

Keep residual stagger.
DEATH_PROMPTS:
DEATH FRAME 0 — FATAL IMPACT.

Strong body jolt.

Head recoils.

One front leg leaves ground.

Legs begin losing support.

Small dark-red torso wound.

DEATH FRAME 1 — BUCKLE.

Body drops.

Abdomen twists.

One middle leg slides.

Head lowers.

Small restrained blood smear.

DEATH FRAME 2 — COLLAPSE.

Body rotates strongly onto one side.

Legs stop supporting weight.

Head drops.

Legs fold or slide.

Moderate dark-red blood.

DEATH FRAME 3 — FINAL FALL.

Body almost fully on ground.

Head low.

All eight legs remain attached and naturally collapsed.

Small-to-moderate blood pool touching body.

DEATH FRAME 4 — DEAD FINAL POSE.

Fully motionless.

Head sideways.

Legs attached and collapsed.

Lifeless or closed eyes.

Torn carapace.

One or two wounds.

Restrained blood pool.

No dismemberment.

No exposed organs.
CORPSE_PROMPTS:
CORPSE VARIANT A.

Dead side-collapse pose.

Body fully on one side.

Head sideways.

Front legs folded.

Middle legs collapsed.

Rear legs splayed.

Lifeless eyes.

Torn carapace.

One wound.

Restrained blood pool.

CORPSE VARIANT B.

Dead belly/side twisted pose.

Head low.

One foreleg extended.

Other forelegs folded.

Uneven middle legs.

Shoulder or flank wound.

Restrained blood smear.

CORPSE VARIANT C.

Dead curled-side pose.

Body slightly curled.

Head tucked low.

Asymmetric forelegs.

One middle leg more stretched.

Legs splayed around body.

Flank wound.

Small blood pool.
